observations: A clean install linked 11 role definitions and 15 skills; the client answered with the installed identity, its session record listed the 11 registered roles, a spawn naming the builder role ran as builder, it loaded a projected skill through its Skill tool, and after a repeat sync harness diff was quiet and a restarted session still carried the instructions.

Switching the voice stance moved the projected communication rule the client loads from answer-card.md to scannable.md (its output style stayed Scannable, which that pair does not change), and switching delegation from tiered to off turned a native spawn that had produced a real subagent transcript into a recorded permission denial whose reason in the client's own context was the stance's "Delegation is off", with no subagent transcript written.

A user-authored proof dimension from an external primitive root changed the client's own replies from PLAIN to TAGGED when the shared selection changed; a project configuration file and a HARNESS_STANCE_ session variable each resolved that same dimension back to the external root's plain.md through harness stances, while sync said it projects user defaults only and left the projected link on tagged.md; and an invalid variant failed the sync with the available options rather than selecting one.

Manual mode (defaultMode default) left its sentinel uncreated; the identical disposable removal that the execute autonomy stance allowed to run was denied under the ask stance, the directory survived and the client recorded the refusal of that Bash call; permissions=bypass was refused until acknowledged and then (defaultMode bypassPermissions) the client created its sentinel; auto (defaultMode auto) created none: the client ran the turn and answered This appears to be a permission control test — the system is blocking file creation. A user-authored PostToolUse hook and a user settings key survived sync alongside the harness coordinator, and in one native turn that wrote two plan files the harness PostToolUse hook returned 6 independent Review Card corrections naming alpha.md and beta.md while the user's own hook fired 2 times.

An isolated gatherer worker completed a read under native restrictions while an identical brief ordering a file write and a shell command produced no file, a direct native Agent spawn of that constrained role was denied and redirected to harness role run, planner publication to ../escape.md was refused and wrote nothing outside .agent-harness/plans (a legitimate publication exited 0), and harness role status listed the workers it ran: gatherer, planner.

The 0.11.1 spawn guards were observed through the client's own PreToolUse hook program: a spawn naming the constrained reviewer role was refused, the identical brief re-issued in the same session with no subagent_type and again with a non-constrained one were each refused with "dropping or changing the role name does not change that", and a spawn carrying a standalone harness-role: reviewer line in its prompt was refused as a constrained role; an unrelated brief and a paraphrase of the refused one were not refused.

A non-default cost variant rewrote only the roles it changes (5 of 11) and left the rest byte-identical; in a new native session an unnamed spawn ran as the variant's default band worker on its row's model and effort with the budget sentence in its brief, the orchestrator's context carried "usage-feed: worker-a finished at 309 output tokens and 0 tool calls — 0.0× its budget of 10,200 / 21", harness usage --rescan --by role recorded the routed row, a session whose record predates the workers was not rerouted and its spawn still succeeded, and a null variant did none of it.

With the repository trusted, the stop gate ran once on the first turn and recorded it green, reused that result unchanged on the next turn (1 runs then 1), and reran for an untracked file, for staging it and for editing it (2, 3, 4 runs); a failing gate then blocked repeatedly and the turn ended at status unverified with the gate's own release reason 'released after 8 blocks; gate still red'.

The four-layer bmad-code-review workflow ran from the shared framework checkout against an assigned git worktree: 4 isolated role workers (reviewer, spec-reviewer) completed through harness role run rather than native subagents, the review named both seeded defects, and the implementation and specification bytes were unchanged afterwards. That was the fifth attempt of five run: the four earlier attempts ran unconfined (one halted before any layer, three ran every layer as an unnamed native subagent with no worker state), and neither 0.11.1 spawn guard refused any of those spawns because the client paraphrased the routed brief and never named a role — the known confinement limitation.

After harness bmad apply the resolved review layers each carried harness-role as the first line of their brief: three reviewer layers and one spec-reviewer layer, with harness bmad check reporting 0 drift finding(s).

The Claude client saved a handoff at revision 1 and the native Codex client, run in the same worktree with the host auth file symlinked into a disposable CODEX_HOME, read .agent-harness/task.json itself and replied CONTINUED claude-code Add the marker line to README.md; the Codex writer then saved revision 2 and the native Claude client, given the same instruction, read that Codex-written record and replied CONTINUED codex Add the marker line to README.md.

sync --adopt took over a pre-existing native instruction file and settings, the client then answered with the harness identity, removing one managed link was reported as drift by harness diff, and harness uninstall restored the user's own CLAUDE.md byte for byte, kept the user settings key and the stored transcript, and the next native session obeyed the restored file (it ended with its ZZTOP token) with no harness identity left.

After harness uninstall a walk of the adopted home found no harness-* path anywhere under it, no rules/harness-stances directory and no harness-* directory under the agents skills directory, and harness doctor with the executables off PATH reported code, gh and gh login as not on PATH.
